findings.evidence: Basic.lean:208 has only the `ofCube` special case `singularChains_map_cubicalToSingular`. The general chain-level form is reproved privately here at line 360 via `(cubicalToSingular k).naturality f`.
findings.fix: Move both to `TauCeti/AlgebraicTopology/Singular/Cubical/Comparison/Basic.lean` as public theorems, e.g. `cubicalToSingular_app_f_map` and `singularChains_d_cubicalToSingular`. Have `singularChains_map_cubicalToSingular` reuse the first.
findings.issue: `comparison_naturality` (naturality of `cubicalToSingular` on arbitrary normalized chains) and `comparison_boundary` (`cubicalToSingular` commutes with `d`/`NormalizedCubicalChain.boundary`) are general facts about the comparison for any `X`, `Y`, not specific to the cube calibration, yet they are `private`.

findings.evidence: The statement has no cube-boundary content. Its proof uses only `TopCat.toSmallSingularSubcomplex_ι` and naturality.
findings.fix: Export it publicly beside `TopCat.toSmallSingularSubcomplex_ι` or in the comparison module.
findings.issue: `comparison_small_inclusion` holds for any `X`, family `F` and `S ⊆ F i`. It is the general compatibility of `toSmallSingularSubcomplex` with the cubical comparison, hidden as `private`.

findings.evidence: The statement takes an arbitrary `P : TopPair`, `c`, `q` and `r`. Its proof only chains `map_ofCube`, `map_boundary_apply`, `map_cubicalBoundaryChainOfCube` and `map_comp`.
findings.fix: Make it public in the module defining `TopPair.cubicalBoundaryChainOfCube` (`Relative/Basic.lean`), next to `map_cubicalBoundaryChainOfCube`.
findings.issue: `boundary_mapped_cube` is a general `TopPair` lemma: the boundary of `q ∘ c` is the pushforward of `cubicalBoundaryChainOfCube` along `r` whenever `q ∘ P.map = r`. It is reusable but `private`.

findings.evidence: Excision.lean:137 has only the `hom` form. The proof here is pure `Iso.eq_comp_inv` manipulation of it, with no cube content.
findings.fix: State it for an arbitrary `P` as a public `TopPair.singularCubicalHomologyIso_inv_singularHomologyδ` in `Comparison/Excision.lean`.
findings.issue: `relative_comparison_inv_δ` is the inverse form of `TopPair.singularCubicalHomologyIso_hom_cubicalHomologyδ` and holds for every pair, but it is private and specialised to `P n`.

findings.fix: Bundle them as `radialHomeomorph : (cubeBoundaryPair n).snd ≃ₜ sphere 0 1`, built from the existing `diskBoundaryPairIsoCube` and `diskBoundaryHomeomorph`. Express `radialMap`/`radialInverse` as its `toFun`/`symm`, or replace them with it.
findings.issue: `radialMap` and `radialInverse` are exported as two separate continuous maps with both inverse laws, but they are not bundled as a homeomorphism `cubeBoundary ≃ₜ sphere`. Consumers must handle the inverse pair by hand and cannot use `Homeomorph` API.

findings.evidence: `upperOverlap_coe` is used manually in `equatorHomotopyEquiv_upperOverlap` and in CubeGenerator `upperCubeMap_on_boundary`, while sibling lemmas `upperInclusion_castSucc` and `upperInclusion_last` are `@[simp]`.
findings.fix: Tag `upperOverlap_coe` `@[simp]`. Tag `radialMap_apply` `@[simp]` too, or drop it once the map is a bundled homeomorphism with its own simp API.
findings.issue: The characterising coercion lemmas `upperOverlap_coe` and `radialMap_apply` (line 61) are not `@[simp]`. Every consumer, including `CubeGenerator.lean`, must `rw` them by name.

summary: Several general facts about the cubical-to-singular comparison and relative cubical chains are hidden as `private` in the calibration file instead of exported from their canonical homes. The radial boundary identification is exposed as two loose inverse maps with no bundled homeomorphism.
